metadata.title: Is Oracle the First AI Casualty as It Sheds 70% of Its Value?

content.text:
Oracle (ORCL) stock has fallen about 70% since its 2025 peak, when the company was worth more than $900 billion. A debt-funded AI buildout has turned free cash flow negative, and the market now values Oracle near $300 billion.
Yet Oracle still reports a $664 billion contracted backlog and expects at least $90 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue. Shareholders and bondholders are supplying the capital to deliver it, through $20 billion in new stock and notes.
Can Oracle Stock Recover While the AI Buildout Burns Cash?
Oracle's value was estimated at $922 billion after a 36% surge on Sept. 10, 2025.
Oracle reported free cash flow of negative $23.7 billion for fiscal 2026. The first quarter of fiscal 2027 added a $5 billion deficit, filings show.
Oracle sold $10 billion of notes on Nov. 4 at coupons of 7% to 8.65%. It also sold $10 billion in stock, an SEC filing shows.
S&P Global Ratings cut Oracle to BBB-, one notch above junk, on July 9. S&P estimates OpenAI accounts for about half of the $638 billion backlog reported then.
Meanwhile, Moody's affirmed Oracle's Baa2 rating with a negative outlook on Nov. 2.
Do Credit Markets See Oracle's Backlog as Safe?
S&P Global Market Intelligence data show Oracle's cost of default insurance hit a record this week. The five-year credit default swap (CDS) spread reached 356 basis points, from below 80 a year earlier.
However, Oracle said on Nov. 20 that its OpenAI contract is fully funded.
The company also targets positive free cash flow in the second half of fiscal 2028, its Investor Day filing shows.
Shares already fell more than 5% on Oct. 8 after a report raised questions about OpenAI's revenue.
The outcome hinges on OpenAI, whose reported $300 billion contract starts in 2027. If payments arrive on schedule, the credit signals may prove overdone.
S&P warns an OpenAI payment shortfall could bind Oracle to data center leases that are hard to unwind. Lenders holding data center loans tied to similar projects could face the same question.
Read the Original story Is Oracle the First AI Casualty as It Sheds 70% of Its Value? by Darryn Pollock at beincrypto.com
